topics.name: Simple past tense (regular and irregular verbs)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Last spring, the little bird lives in a shell.
Last spring, the little bird living in a shell.
Last spring, the little bird lived in a shell.
questions.rule: Last spring is in the past, so use the past tense: lived.
Eggs is plural, so use were. Use was for one thing.

options: The cat is sleeping under of the tree.
The cat is sleeping under the tree.
The cat is sleeping the under tree.
questions.rule: A preposition comes before its noun, alone: under the tree.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two days ago shows the past, so fly becomes flew.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Those leaves is plural, so use were, not was.
When we compare two things with than, use the -er form: bluer.
under shows that something is below something else: under its mother's wings.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past tense.
questions.rule: flew is the past form of fly. Subject + verb + place: The bird flew out of the nest.

options: I were in the park with my cousin.
I am in the park with my cousin yesterday.
I was in the park with my cousin.
questions.rule: With I in the past, use was: I was in the park.

chat: Which is the tallest tree in your school?
options: The neem tree is the most tallest.
The neem tree is the tallest.
The neem tree is the more taller.
questions.rule: Short adjectives take -est alone: the tallest. Never add most or more as well.

options: The bird thought the world was made of straw.
The bird thinked the world was made of straw.
The bird think the world was made of straw.
questions.rule: think is irregular: its past form is thought.

options: The nest sat between two thin branch.
The nest sat between to two thin branches.
The nest sat between two thin branches.
questions.rule: between comes straight before the two things, and two needs a plural: branches.

options: This nest is more small than that one.
This nest is smaller than that one.
This nest is smallest than that one.
questions.rule: For two things, add -er to a short adjective and use than: smaller than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Birds and clouds are in the sky, not on the sky.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: saw tells us the story is in the past, so take must be took.

questions.after: small and round for the baby bird.
questions.rule: The world is one thing, so the past form is was.
Yesterday shows the past: sit becomes sat.
The preposition in comes before the tree to show the place.

chat: Did you see the parrot in the garden?
options: Yes, I seen it on the guava tree.
Yes, I see it on the guava tree yesterday.
Yes, I saw it on the guava tree.
questions.rule: Answer a Did question in the simple past: I saw. Seen needs has/have.

options: It is under in the sofa.
questions.rule: Use one preposition, placed before the noun: under the sofa.

options: The mother bird was busy, and the babies were hungry.
The mother bird were busy, and the babies were hungry.
The mother bird was busy, and the babies was hungry.
questions.rule: One bird takes was; many babies take were.

options: Of all the birds, the peacock has the longer tail.
Of all the birds, the peacock has the most long tail.
Of all the birds, the peacock has the longest tail.
questions.rule: Of all compares more than two, so use the -est form: the longest.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With than we compare two things, so use the -er form: stronger than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: All the stars is plural and last night is past, so use were.
between is used for a place in the middle of two things.

questions.after: of all the eggs in the nest.
questions.rule: Of all means more than two, so use the smallest.
In a question, were comes before you: Where were you?
found is the past form of find. Who + did what + where.

chat: Was the bird park crowded today?
options: No, it is quite empty yesterday.
questions.rule: It is singular, so in the past use was: it was quite empty.

chat: Which kite flew higher, yours or mine?
options: Yours flew more higher than mine.
questions.rule: Two kites are compared, so use higher than. Don't add more before an -er word.

options: An owl lives into a hole in an old tree.
An owl lives in a hole between an old tree.
An owl lives in a hole in an old tree.
questions.rule: An owl lives in a hole: in = inside. Into shows movement, and between needs two things.

options: The children saw three sparrows on the wall.
The childs saw three sparrows on the wall.
The children seen three sparrows on the wall.
questions.rule: The plural of child is children, and the past of see is saw.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: My friends and I means many people, so use were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two actions joined by and keep the same tense: hopped ... and looked.

questions.after: an owl on the old banyan tree.
questions.rule: Two days ago is past, so use saw. Seen needs has/have before it.

questions.after: on the floor of the cage this morning.
questions.rule: These feathers is plural, so use were.
brother's shows whose kite it is; bigger than compares two kites.
Wh-word + is + subject + -ing verb; under the bed tells the place.

chat: What did you see on your trip to the hills?
options: We seen many eagles and a waterfall.
We saw many eagles and a waterfall.
We saw many eagle and a waterfall.
questions.rule: Use the simple past saw, and many takes a plural noun: eagles.

chat: Thank you for the bird book. Was it expensive?
options: No, it were not expensive at all.
No, it was not expensive at all.
No, it not was expensive at all.
questions.rule: It takes was, and not comes after it: it was not.

options: The bird flown beyond the tree and saw that the sky was blue.
The bird flew beyond the tree and saw that the sky was blue.
The bird flew beyond the tree and see that the sky was blue.
questions.rule: Both actions are past: flew and saw. Flown needs has/had.

options: The world outside the nest was more bigger and brighter than the bird had thought.
The world outside the nest was biggest and brighter than the bird had thought.
The world outside the nest was bigger and brighter than the bird had thought.
questions.rule: With than, both adjectives take -er: bigger and brighter. Never more + -er.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The whole world is singular, so use was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: We say in the morning but at sunset, at night.

questions.after: beyond the tree and saw the wide blue sky.
questions.rule: saw is past, so the first verb must match: flew.

questions.rule: Of all compares many things, so use the sweetest (never most + -est).
Wh-word + were + plural subject: Why were the little birds so quiet?
the highest of all compares Mira's kite with all the other kites.

chat: You came home late. What happened?
options: Yes, it breaked down near the market, so I walked.
Yes, it broke down near the market, so I walked.
Yes, it broke down near the market, so I walk.
questions.rule: break is irregular: past broke. Both actions are past: broke ... walked.

chat: I can't find the bird feeder. Where did you put it?
options: I hung it on the hook between of the two windows.
I hung it on the hook between the two windows.
I hung it in the hook among the two windows.
questions.rule: Things hang on a hook, and for two things use between with no extra word.
